title: GCB design system: token cleanup milestone
author: Digital Transformation Team (User Experience)

subtitle_lines: What changed in the Figma libraries, how Figma now matches the code,
cover.prepared_by: Prepared by Digital Transformation Team (User Experience)

pages.title: Milestone summary
cols: The design system now holds only what every GCB product needs. Published variables fell from 442 to 161, and Figma matches the code's values.
Split the tokens into design system and project layers, removed what only Internet Banking uses, and synced Figma to the code.
A small core is easier to learn and to keep in step with code. New GCB products can start from it without inheriting one project's history.
Figma and code agree on colour, radius and motion.
Amber and Smoke brands switch with one mode.
Figma work is complete for this milestone. The code split and the shared token package are next.
A GCB GitHub organisation for the package, and four design questions listed at the end.

pages.title: Why we cleaned up
cols: The first version of the Figma library was copied from the Internet Banking code, so it carried one project's details into the design system.
442 variables, all published. 79 were illustration colours and 47 were Internet Banking components such as the hero and tiles.
Eight core colours, the radius scale and the motion values no longer matched the code.
An earlier cleanup removed the smoke and black button colours because the code did not use them, so the Smoke button had turned amber.
There was no clean way to add a second brand or a second product without copying everything again.
A core that every GCB product shares.
Project tokens kept with the project.
Brand as a switch, not a copy.
Figma and code reading the same values.

pages.title: Figma and code aligned
left: lead
The code is the source of truth for values. Figma was synced to it.
p
The written rules were updated to match too, so all three now agree.
after: The code itself has not been restructured yet. The token package that will generate both Figma and code values is the next phase.

pages.title: Brands and buttons
cols: Brand is now a switch. Personal banking uses Amber and business banking uses Smoke, from the same components.
Primary, hover and the text on primary follow the Brand mode. A frame set to Smoke turns every primary button ash, with no copies.
Calendar days, selected menu rows and Tertiary buttons now follow the brand too.
Brand alt: the other brand colour.
Neutral: black, white in dark mode.
Neutral inverse: white, black in dark mode.
Tested on real buttons in Amber and Smoke, light and dark.
Icons have their own three tokens, primary, secondary and on primary, so designers can pick an icon colour from the picker.
Brand alt and the neutral buttons exist in Figma. They reach the code with the token package.

pages.title: Adding colours in new projects
cols: New products start from the core and add only what they need. Ask these in order and stop at the first yes.
1. Does a token already mean this?
Use it. Most new colours end here.
Add a Brand mode, plus a colour ramp if the hue is new.
Make a local token in the project's own file. The design system does not change.
Keep it in the illustration, not in tokens.
A token moves into the core only when a second product needs it.
Core names never include a brand, hue or product.
A dark frame must set both Theme and NIBS to Dark.

pages.title: What comes next
left: lead
The Figma side is in good shape. The next milestone moves the same structure into code.

rows: Separate core and project tokens in globals.css, with no visual change
Publish @gcb/tokens so every project imports the same values
Generate Figma values from the package instead of by hand
Add Brand alt, Neutral and Neutral inverse to the Button
Share components the same way, once a second product starts

pages.title: Decisions needed
cols: One setup decision unblocks the next milestone. Four design questions are open.
The package needs a GCB organisation on GitHub to be published as @gcb/tokens. The code currently sits under a personal account.
Menu surfaces and four badge text colours differ slightly from the core. Merge them, or keep them.
Text in Mobile mode switches to DM Sans, but the house rule is Open Sans everywhere. Which is right?
Figma components use Lucide icons; the house rule says Material Symbols.
The code makes this colour red in dark mode, which looks like a mistake.
